description.value: We investigated the association of cigarette smoking and regional gray and white matter volume by using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for T1-weighted high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging in 315 current-smokers and 659 never-smokers from the representative Study of Health in Pomerania (SHIP).

description.value: As this study is cross-sectional, we cannot exclude the possibility of any preexisting structural differences between the analyzed smokers and never-smokers.

definition.value: Current-smokers showed significant smaller regional GM volume compared with never-smokers and controlled for age, gender, and alcohol consumption.

spans.text: Current-smokers showed significant smaller regional GM volume in the right DLPFC comprising the dorsal parts of the superior and middle frontal gyrus; in the bilateral DMPFC, in the bilateral VLPFC comprising the orbital part of the superior, middle, and inferior frontal gyrus; and in the bilateral ventromedial prefrontal gyrus (VMPFC) comprising the orbital part of the medial frontal gyrus and the rectal gyrus compared with never-smokers and controlled for age, gender, and alcohol consumption (see Table 2 , Figure 1 ).

value: Our study showed that in current-smokers smoking is significantly associated with gray matter volume loss in the prefrontal cortex, the anterior cingulate cortex, the insula, and the olfactory gyrus.
There were no regions where current-smokers showed more GM volume than never-smokers.

spans.text: Our study showed that in current-smokers smoking is significantly associated with gray matter volume loss in the prefrontal cortex, the anterior cingulate cortex, the insula, and the olfactory gyrus.
A statistical threshold of p <0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons using the Family-wise Error (FWE) rate across the whole brain on voxel level was applied for obtaining the results.
